title: Violin traded for a C-melody saxophone and lessons
summary: He gave up the violin for a Wurlitzer C-melody saxophone, took lessons from a Bohemian clarinetist and was soon invited to play paid jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: But I did want to get an instrument early. I wanted to take lessons. First of all, they got me a fiddle, got me a violin. You know a violin, if you wanted to get any sounds out of it, it was going to take your three or four years before you could make the sounds, and it was nothing more -- except what Charlie Margulis used to say, mice. So I traded that in soon for a Wurlitzer, a C-melody saxophone. I'd watch the ads.
I was, let's say, I would say 15, 14 or 15. [PAUSE]
The C-melody saxophone, well, you know, the Metronome. My sister used to get the Metronome and I'd look through it, and there was always a Wurlitzer ad in there
and tell you that the C-melody saxophone was coming along, you didn't have to transpose, it was all over, and it was no trouble reading, no trouble playing it in no time.

So after the violin this seemed like it would be a pretty good switch to me, so I got one nice shiny gold bell, and I wanted to take lessons this time and learn it right, so I went down to an old clarinet player, a Czechoslovakian. Bohemian he told me, came over and settled in the town and he had a son who played trumpet and another son who played oboe and his daughter would play the piano, and it was a musical family and he had a good musical background, so I went down and he gave me lessons.

Particularly how to blow it, long low tones and I got within a short time, I got a pretty good tone on it and I could -- it was very easy to finger, you know, it's not like the clarinet, where the octave is more than an octave -- this is an octave and it's an octave.

So it was really fairly easy to learn and I don't think I had it a month or more where I was blowing it, still taking lessons, but some of the local guys came around and wanted to know if I wanted to come around and play with them. So one of them came around and told me that they had a job and I'd come along and play. Get paid for it.
